newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICA CRUSH ARGENTINA 46-15.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICA CRUSH ARGENTINA 46-15.

text.p: South Africa overcame a slow start to easily beat Argentina 46-15 in a seven tries to two romp in the first of two rugby union tests at the Ferro Carril Oeste stadium on Saturday.
The Springboks finished the match with a flurry, three of their tries coming in the last 12 minutes.
With 33 minutes of the match gone, Argentina's Jose Luis Cilley and South Africa's Henry Honiball had only managed one penalty goal apiece.
The Pumas broke through for the first try in the 35th minute when Gonzalo Camardon cracked the Springboks' defence, but he was injured in the process and had to be replaced by Eduardo Simone.

Argentina's solid defence withered in the dying stages of the half allowing Andre Venter and Mark Andrews to cross over. Honiball converted both tries for the world champions to take a 17-8 lead into the second period.
Springbok centre Hennie Le Roux extended the lead shortly after the break to effectively settle the game.
The tourists increased their lead to 29-8 when they were awarded a penalty try which Honiball converted.
Argentina gave their home supporters something to cheer when Rolando Martin scored and Cilley's conversion reduced South Africa's lead to 14 points.
The Springboks quelled any thoughts of an Argentina fight back, with James Small, scrumhalf Joost Van Der Westhuizen and full-back Andre Joubert, all running in late tries.

South Africa: Dawie Theron, James Dalton, Adrian Garvey, Kobus Wiese, Mark Andrews, Ruben Kruger, Andre Venter, Gary Teichmann, Joost Van Der Westhuizen, Henry Honiball, Jacques Olivier, Hennie Le Roux, Japie Mulder, Franco Smith, Andre Joubert. (Replacements: Toks Van Der Linke, James Small).

Argentina: Roberto Grau, Federico Mendez, Omar Hasan Jalil, Pedro Sporleder, German Llanes, Rolando Martin, Raul Perez, Pablo Camerlinck, Nicolas Fernandez Miranda, Jose Luis Cilley, Tomas Solari, Lisandro Arbizu, Gonzalo Camardon, Octavio Bartolucci, Facundo Soler. (Replacement: Eduardo Simone).
